text:
For the reader interested in more specific analysis of unavoidable air pollution impacts, the environmental impact statement prepared by the Montana State Department of Health and Environmental Sciences for the Generating Plant at Colstrip provides a listing of harmful effects. In short, it is evident that whether or not the emissions meet air quality standards, the long-term effects may include severe stresses to plants, animals and workers.
Land required for a plant and associated facilities would be taken from agricultural production for an indefinite period. The plant site probably would require 500 to 1,000 acres. This acreage also would be lost as wildlife habitat.
Operation of a conversion plant would require an estimated 16,000 acre feet of process and cooling water annually. This water then would be unavailable for other uses. Plant operation would result in significant increases in noise levels, which might be annoying to local residents and possibly injurious to workers not using protective devices.
Construction of a conversion plant would require a large construction force, which would place a severe strain on facilities and housing in Hardin and other nearby communities. Such an influx might also be detrimental to the culture and way of life of the Crow Indians. Upon completion of construction activities, the majority of the construction force would leave the area, possibly resulting in surplus housing and facilities and depressed economic conditions.
